title: Control-plane subnet affinity policy and conditional DNS proxying for cross-VPC control plane
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds a zone-aware affinity allocator for control-plane subnets with a conditional DNS proxying component to allow cross-VPC resolver handoff. Backwards compatible; opt-in policy via installer config. Improves control-plane stability during AZ drain and multi-account setups.
description: Context: Customers running Redwood Private across multiple VPCs and accounts have seen control-plane flakiness when control-plane endpoints and control-plane instances are scattered across AZs and when cross-VPC DNS forwarding is not consistently available. This PR implements a deterministic affinity policy for allocating control-plane subnets (prefer stickiness to preferred AZs and capacity pools) and adds a conditional DNS proxying helper that automates resolver handoff for hosted/private route scenarios. Motivation: reduce cross-AZ control-plane chattiness, avoid hot-spotting of ephemeral endpoints during rolling upgrades, and make DNS handoff deterministic for cross-account control-plane peering. What changed (high level): 1) Introduce a subnet-affinity policy module used by the installer to pick or create control-plane subnets based on zone scores, capacity tags, and historical allocations. The allocator prefers keeping existing allocations stable during upgrades unless an explicit "rebalance" flag is set. 2) Add a lightweight dns-proxy-controller that can be optionally enabled in the control-plane VPC; the controller programs conditional forward rules (Route 53 Resolver rules or on-prem DNS proxy entries) to point consumer VPCs to the nearest control-plane endpoint IPs and includes TTL-based failover. 3) Security hardening: automatic security-group templates for control-plane endpoints that limit port exposure, explicit IAM policy additions for the DNS controller to manage resolver rules, and audit log hooks. 4) Installer CLI flags and Helm values: new flags --subnet-affinity-mode (off|preferred|strict), --dns-proxy-enabled (true|false), and helm values under controlplane.affinity and controlplane.dnsProxy. 5) Tests and infra: unit tests for allocator heuristics, an integration harness using localstack for resolver rule emulation, and Terraform module updates to surface the new options. Rollout plan: feature is off by default. Admins can opt-in via installer config; rolling upgrade path preserves current allocations unless --subnet-affinity-mode=strict is specified. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in ENG-1973) - [x] Terraform module changes - [x] Helm chart values and templates - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] E2E smoke in staging - [x] Docs updates (quickstart/upgrade notes) Backwards compatibility: installing without opt-in preserves existing behavior. Strict affinity mode may reallocate subnets if explicitly requested by operators. See release_notes for upgrade guidance. Related: ENG-1973, PM-381, SUP-4421.

María Rossi: Verified RBAC scope for the dns controller; left one small comment about retry backoff for resolver rule APIs.

merge_result: Merged via squash on 2026-02-24 by Priya Natarajan. Commit message consolidated allocator + dns proxy changes. No post-merge hotfix required. Changelog entry added under Unreleased.
notes_for_ops: Operator notes: when enabling strict affinity in a live cluster, run installer with --dry-run first to preview subnet reassignments. If dns-proxy-enabled=true is used across accounts, ensure the SUP-4421 cross-account resolver IAM role is provisioned. TTL for conditional forwarders defaults to 60s and can be tuned via controlplane.dnsProxy.ttl.
testing_summary: Unit: allocator heuristics covered with synthetic zone/capacity inputs. Integration: localstack-based resolver tests validated create/update/delete of conditional forward rules. Staging: deployed to two region staging clusters with cross-VPC peering; observed stable control-plane during simulated AZ drain.
